children: is partnering with Amazon’s Web Services
to create Star Wars-themed, AI-powered robots that can interact with each other—and guests—to take Disney animatronics to the next level.
Designed by Disney Imagineers and powered by AWS, the Anzellans—an alien species featured in
– will debut at the Amazon re:Invent event in Las Vegas from November 30 to December 4.

Using Amazon Bedrock and the Kiro coding agent, Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a, and Jibu Bre’a will each have cameras, microphones, and sensors to react to each other and guests in real time. The robots will be programmed with pre-recorded lines in both English and Anzellan, and the AI selects which phrases to use based on each character's personality.

“What makes this innovation truly special is that it exemplifies physical AI: every word, every gesture, and every personality trait was crafted by Disney’s Imagineers—with AWS powering the real-time decision-making that brings those creative choices to life,” said Samira Panah Bakhtiar, general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games Advertising, and Sports for AWS.
The Anzellans are not the first next-generation robots Disney has in its employ. Built with NVIDIA

franchise debuted at Disneyland Paris’s World of Frozen in March 2026, while the bipedal Star Wars BDX droids are integrated with FieldAI to help them roam safely around guests at Disneyland’s Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge park. Disney also uses AI-powered robots as parking assistants at its theme parks to direct drivers to open parking spaces.

title: Disney Imagineers and AWS create AI-powered Anzellan robots
